articles.headline: No. 16 Washington women beat Stanford 105-50, the Cardinal's worst loss in program history
articles.description: — Brynn McGaughy scored a career-high 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 points on 7-of-10 shooting and No. 16 Washington handed Stanford its worst loss in program history, beating the Cardinal 105-50 on Friday night.

articles.headline: JuJu Watkins takes over, scores season-high 36 to rally No. 4 USC past Baylor
articles.description: JuJu Watkins had 36 points and 11 rebounds as No. 4 USC came back from an early 15-point deficit to beat Baylor 78-69 on Friday night.

articles.headline: No. 4 USC rallies from 15 down behind JuJu Watkins to beat Baylor 78-69 at Intuit Dome
articles.description: — JuJu Watkins scored a season-high 36 points and No. 4 Southern California rallied from an early 15-point deficit to beat Baylor 78-69 on Friday night at the Hollywood Hardwood Classic in the first women's college basketball game played at Intuit Dome.

article.headline: Clara Strack scores 29 to go with career-high 18 boards as No. 12 Kentucky women beat EMU 81-47

article.story: LEXINGTON, Ky. -- — Clara Strack scored 29 points to go with a career-high 18 rebounds and No. 12 Kentucky beat Eastern Michigan 81-47 on Sunday. Strack was 8 of 14 from the field, with four made 3-pointers, and 9 of 10 at the free-throw line. Me’Arah O’Neal and Asia Boone each added three 3-pointers, and Kentucky finished 14 of 29 from 3-point range — after making 18, 18 and 12 in the previous three games. O’Neal and Savvy Swords each had 12 points, and Boone scored 11 for Kentucky, which has opened a season 5-0 for the third straight year. Peyton Hill scored 16 points and Fernanda Ovalle added 10 for Eastern Michigan (0-4). Kentucky started the game on a 19-0 run and the score was 25-2 at the end of the first quarter. Strack scored Kentucky's opening eight points of the second quarter to make it 33-13. Then, Strack scored 10 points during an 18-0 run to begin the third for a 61-23 lead as EMU missed 13 straight shots spanning halftime. Kentucky's lead reached 46 points early in the fourth. Up next Eastern Michigan: Plays at Oakland on Wednesday.
